command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e and `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it
# (spawn#707), so errexit is off and statuses are checked by hand.

ACC=ERR15105294
API="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport?accession=$ACC&result=read_run"

echo "== ask ENA for the paths; never construct them =="
# The vol1/fastq/<prefix>/<subdir>/ layout is not something to guess, and ENA also hands
# back a per-file md5 plus its own read/base counts. Same discipline as recipes/flye.
curl -fsS "$API&fields=fastq_ftp,fastq_md5,read_count,base_count,library_strategy,library_selection&format=tsv" -o rep.tsv
col() { awk -F'\t' -v want="$1" 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i==want) c=i; next} NR==2{print $c}' rep.tsv; }
FTP=$(col fastq_ftp); MD5=$(col fastq_md5)
STRAT=$(col library_strategy); SEL=$(col library_selection)
echo "library	$STRAT / $SEL"
# MetaPhlAn maps to clade-specific markers, so an AMPLICON library hits almost none of
# them: it processes every read, exits 0, and reports no species. Assert the strategy.
test "$STRAT" = "WGS" || { echo "$ACC is $STRAT, not WGS"; exit 1; }
# NOT a check on library_selection: PCR there means the library prep amplified, which is
# routine and still whole-genome. library_strategy is the discriminator that matters.

echo "== fetch; the md5 is the gate, not the byte count =="
# MEASURED, and it corrects an assumption: EBI to us-west-2 ran at 0.8 MB/s, SLOWER than a
# home connection. The 18.2 MB/s seen elsewhere in this recipe was unitn.it in Italy, not
# EBI -- one host says nothing about another. That is why this fixture is 117 MB rather than
# the 2.97 GB run: at 0.8 MB/s the larger one costs an hour of instance time per attempt.
i=1; OK=1
for u in ${FTP//;/ }; do
  m=$(echo "$MD5" | cut -d";" -f$i)
  f="${ACC}_$i.fastq.gz"
  T0=$(date +%s)
  curl -fL --no-progress-meter --retry 5 --retry-delay 10 -o "$f" "https://$u"
  RC=$?; T1=$(date +%s)
  SZ=$(stat -c%s "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  awk -v r=$RC -v s=$((T1-T0)) -v b=$SZ -v f="$f" 'BEGIN{printf "%s\trc=%d %ds %.0f MB %.1f MB/s\n", f, r, s, b/1e6, (s>0? b/1e6/s : 0)}'
  echo "$m  $f" > "$f.want.md5"
  md5sum -c "$f.want.md5" || { echo "md5 MISMATCH on $f"; OK=0; }
  i=$((i+1))
done
test "$OK" = "1" || { echo "one or more files failed their published md5"; exit 1; }
echo "md5	both files match ENA published checksums"

echo "== independent cross-check on the transfer: ENA own counts =="
# A truncated FASTQ is still valid gzip and would still profile, into a quietly worse
# answer. Counting reads is a second, independent check on top of the md5.
R1=$(zcat ${ACC}_1.fastq.gz | awk 'END{print NR/4}')
R2=$(zcat ${ACC}_2.fastq.gz | awk 'END{print NR/4}')
echo "reads_r1	$R1"; echo "reads_r2	$R2"
ENA_READS=$(col read_count)
echo "ena_read_count	$ENA_READS"
test "$R1" = "$R2" || { echo "mates disagree: $R1 vs $R2"; exit 1; }
# ENA reports the total across both mates for a paired run.
awk -v a="$R1" -v e="$ENA_READS" 'BEGIN{ if (2*a != e) { printf "read count mismatch: 2x%d != %d\n", a, e; exit 1 } }' || exit 1
echo "counts	2 x $R1 == $ENA_READS as ENA reports"
echo "STAGE OK"
